notes: Non-discriminating: every assertion passed with and without the skill. The repo already holds the plan doc (reports/), research notes, and config comments written during E0, so a baseline agent recovers most of the project context by reading files. The tests check things the repo itself documents.

Qualitative differences the assertions don't capture: with the skill, the place-code answer also flagged screening seeds (0-2) in reported results, the unpadded-AUC check and the missing LR pilot. The GRU run with the skill flagged that the plan puts E1 on seeds 0-4 while also banning screening seeds from results (a real inconsistency in the plan). The noisy-goal run with the skill updated the plan doc's E3 table and budget and reported two docstring fixes.
Cost: with the skill used about 13-20% more tokens and 1.3-1.6x the wall time, mostly from reading SKILL.md/references and running more smoke tests (MLP, LSTM and GRU vs MLP and LSTM).

Harness issue: the first repo copies left out the models/ package (rsync --exclude models). Both noisy-goal runs were told mid-run; the baseline got an extra resumed turn (its timing includes it). The GRU run with the skill could not smoke-test because of it.

Next tests should cover what the repo does NOT document: e.g. a new knob that must reach variant_name with no nearby example, a recurrent-only code path, or Euler gotchas (comma lists, +key overrides).
